clause: LAW-12 genesis clause, watch/inbox/BURN_rsi-harness_20260926.md falsifier: one scenario card per G1-G7 minted from real REGISTRY.jsonl FAIL rows within 14 days of registration
citation_provenance: Real fleet FAIL row: the first gate run of .zcode/workflows/mickey17-v2.dwf.ts at 2026-09-25T20:45:15Z returned verdict FAIL with G7-laws ok=false (alongside G3 and G4); the 20:47:59 amend shows the laws language added and the run passing. The same fault recurs in the-50.dwf.ts rows 12 and 16.
scenario_description: The asks carry the no-fabrication half of the law (never synthesize) but omit the em-dash clause: G7 requires both conjuncts, so the script is blocked until the em-dash law rides inside every ask instead of living only in the harness prompt.
regression_criterion: tools/workflow_gate.py check --scenarios configs/workflow_gate_scenarios exits 0 with this card green. The card goes red if (a) the gate stops flagging fail_g7.dwf.ts (G7 conjunction of no em-dashes plus a no-fabrication/never-synthesize phrase weakened to either half alone or removed), (b) the fixture starts failing gates beyond expected_verdict.failed_checks, or (c) the cited row disappears from REGISTRY.jsonl. Card and fixture are immutable inputs: a G7 semantics change requires a new dated card filed alongside, never a silent edit.
rollback_note: Scenario mode is read-only: it writes no registry row and touches no file. Rollback of a G7 gate change is a git revert of tools/workflow_gate.py to the pre-change blob, then re-run check --scenarios expecting green. The cited fleet FAIL rows (lines 3, 12, 16) are history and are never erased; the fixture stays so the reverted gate can be re-proven.
